description.en: Your body measurements and all your laboratory results (blood, urine and other samples), including pregnancy and fertility hormones, semen analyses, and intimate observations such as vaginal bleeding and cervical mucus.
description.fr: Vos mesures corporelles et tous vos résultats d'analyses (sang, urines et autres prélèvements), y compris les hormones de grossesse et de fertilité, les analyses de sperme et des observations intimes comme les saignements vaginaux et la glaire cervicale.
description.es: Sus medidas corporales y todos sus resultados de laboratorio (sangre, orina y otras muestras), incluidas las hormonas del embarazo y de la fertilidad, los análisis de semen y observaciones íntimas como el sangrado vaginal y el moco cervical.
description.it: Le sue misure corporee e tutti i suoi risultati di laboratorio (sangue, urine e altri campioni), compresi gli ormoni della gravidanza e della fertilità, gli spermiogrammi e le osservazioni intime come il sanguinamento vaginale e il muco cervicale.
description.pt-BR: Suas medidas corporais e todos os seus resultados de exames (sangue, urina e outras amostras), incluindo hormônios da gravidez e da fertilidade, espermogramas e observações íntimas, como sangramento vaginal e muco cervical.

description.en: Blood test results that have no field of their own, which can include infectious disease tests (such as HIV or hepatitis), viral loads and drug levels.
description.fr: Résultats d'analyses de sang qui n'ont pas de champ dédié, pouvant inclure des analyses de maladies infectieuses (comme le VIH ou les hépatites), des charges virales et des dosages de médicaments.
description.es: Resultados de análisis de sangre que no tienen un campo propio, entre los que pueden figurar pruebas de enfermedades infecciosas (como VIH o hepatitis), cargas virales y niveles de medicamentos.
description.it: Risultati di esami del sangue che non hanno un campo proprio, tra cui possono rientrare test per malattie infettive (come HIV o epatite), cariche virali e dosaggi di farmaci.
description.pt-BR: Resultados de exames de sangue que não têm campo próprio, podendo incluir testes de doenças infecciosas (como HIV ou hepatite), cargas virais e dosagens de medicamentos.

description.en: Includes basal (waking) temperatures recorded for fertility charting, and whether a reading was disturbed.
description.fr: Comprend les températures basales (au réveil) relevées pour le suivi de la fertilité, et si une mesure a été perturbée.
description.es: Incluye las temperaturas basales (al despertar) registradas para el seguimiento de la fertilidad, y si una medición se vio alterada.
description.it: Comprende le temperature basali (al risveglio) registrate per il monitoraggio della fertilità, e se una misurazione è stata alterata.
description.pt-BR: Inclui as temperaturas basais (ao acordar) registradas para o acompanhamento da fertilidade, e se uma medição foi alterada.

description.en: Urine test results that have no field of their own, which can include infectious disease tests and drug screening.
description.fr: Résultats d'analyses d'urine qui n'ont pas de champ dédié, pouvant inclure des analyses de maladies infectieuses et des dépistages de drogues ou de médicaments.
description.es: Resultados de análisis de orina que no tienen un campo propio, entre los que pueden figurar pruebas de enfermedades infecciosas y detección de drogas.
description.it: Risultati di esami delle urine che non hanno un campo proprio, tra cui possono rientrare test per malattie infettive e screening di droghe o farmaci.
description.pt-BR: Resultados de exames de urina que não têm campo próprio, podendo incluir testes de doenças infecciosas e triagem de drogas.

description.en: Results of a cerebrospinal fluid test, which can include tests for infections.
description.fr: Résultats d'une analyse du liquide céphalorachidien, pouvant inclure la recherche d'infections.
description.es: Resultados de un análisis del líquido cefalorraquídeo, que puede incluir pruebas de infecciones.
description.it: Risultati di un esame del liquido cerebrospinale, tra cui possono rientrare test per infezioni.
description.pt-BR: Resultados de um exame do líquido cefalorraquidiano, podendo incluir pesquisa de infecções.

description.en: The questions and proposed values a contact sends you in a conversation, and your answers. Never included when you share all your data: each contact reads only its own conversation.
description.fr: Les questions et les valeurs proposées qu'un contact vous envoie dans une conversation, et vos réponses. Jamais inclus quand vous partagez toutes vos données : chaque contact ne lit que sa propre conversation.
description.es: Las preguntas y los valores propuestos que un contacto le envía en una conversación, y sus respuestas. Nunca se incluyen cuando comparte todos sus datos: cada contacto lee solo su propia conversación.
description.it: Le domande e i valori proposti che un contatto le invia in una conversazione, e le sue risposte. Mai inclusi quando condivide tutti i suoi dati: ogni contatto legge solo la propria conversazione.
description.pt-BR: As perguntas e os valores propostos que um contato envia a você em uma conversa, e as suas respostas. Nunca incluídos quando você compartilha todos os seus dados: cada contato lê apenas a sua própria conversa.

description.en: Every medical document you keep, filed or not: reports, letters, results, consents, advance directives, donor and emergency cards, images and administrative papers, including sensitive ones.
description.fr: Tous les documents médicaux que vous conservez, classés ou non : rapports, lettres, résultats, consentements, directives anticipées, cartes de donneur et d'urgence, images et papiers administratifs, y compris les plus sensibles.
description.es: Todos los documentos médicos que conserva, archivados o no: informes, cartas, resultados, consentimientos, instrucciones previas, tarjetas de donante y de emergencia, imágenes y papeles administrativos, incluidos los sensibles.
description.it: Tutti i documenti medici che conserva, archiviati o no: referti, lettere, risultati, consensi, disposizioni anticipate di trattamento, tessere di donatore e di emergenza, immagini e documenti amministrativi, compresi quelli sensibili.
description.pt-BR: Todos os documentos médicos que você guarda, arquivados ou não: relatórios, cartas, resultados, consentimentos, diretivas antecipadas, cartões de doador e de emergência, imagens e papéis administrativos, inclusive os sensíveis.

description.en: Documents about your care: reports, letters, prescriptions, results, plans, certificates, consents, advance directives, donor and emergency cards, images and recordings, including sensitive ones.
description.fr: Documents sur vos soins : rapports, lettres, ordonnances, résultats, plans, certificats, consentements, directives anticipées, cartes de donneur et d'urgence, images et enregistrements, y compris les plus sensibles.
description.es: Documentos sobre su atención: informes, cartas, recetas, resultados, planes, certificados, consentimientos, instrucciones previas, tarjetas de donante y de emergencia, imágenes y grabaciones, incluidos los sensibles.
description.it: Documenti sulle sue cure: referti, lettere, prescrizioni, risultati, piani, certificati, consensi, disposizioni anticipate di trattamento, tessere di donatore e di emergenza, immagini e registrazioni, compresi quelli sensibili.
description.pt-BR: Documentos sobre os seus cuidados: relatórios, cartas, receitas, resultados, planos, atestados, consentimentos, diretivas antecipadas, cartões de doador e de emergência, imagens e gravações, inclusive os sensíveis.

description.en: Papers around your care, such as invoices, appointment letters and insurance documents. They can show which care you received.
description.fr: Papiers autour de vos soins, comme les factures, les convocations et les documents d'assurance. Ils peuvent montrer quels soins vous avez reçus.
description.es: Papeles relacionados con su atención, como facturas, citaciones y documentos del seguro. Pueden mostrar qué atención ha recibido.
description.it: Documenti legati alle sue cure, come fatture, lettere di appuntamento e documenti assicurativi. Possono mostrare quali cure ha ricevuto.
description.pt-BR: Papéis em torno dos seus cuidados, como faturas, cartas de agendamento e documentos do plano de saúde. Eles podem mostrar quais cuidados você recebeu.

description.en: Papers from and for insurers: policies, cards, cost approvals, reimbursement statements. They can show which care you received.
description.fr: Papiers des assureurs et pour eux : polices, cartes, garanties de prise en charge, décomptes de prestations. Ils peuvent montrer quels soins vous avez reçus.
description.es: Papeles de las aseguradoras y para ellas: pólizas, tarjetas, autorizaciones de cobertura, liquidaciones de reembolso. Pueden mostrar qué atención ha recibido.
description.it: Documenti delle assicurazioni e per le assicurazioni: polizze, tessere, autorizzazioni di spesa, rendiconti dei rimborsi. Possono mostrare quali cure ha ricevuto.
description.pt-BR: Papéis das operadoras e para elas: apólices, carteirinhas, autorizações de cobertura, extratos de reembolso. Eles podem mostrar quais cuidados você recebeu.

label.pt-BR: Atendimentos, profissionais e serviços de saúde

description.en: Your consultations, hospital stays and other care visits, with the doctors and places involved and the reason given, including sensitive visits.
description.fr: Vos consultations, séjours hospitaliers et autres soins, avec les médecins et les lieux concernés et le motif indiqué, y compris les visites sensibles.
description.es: Sus consultas, hospitalizaciones y otras visitas de atención, con los médicos y lugares implicados y el motivo indicado, incluidas las visitas sensibles.
description.it: Le sue consultazioni, i ricoveri ospedalieri e altre visite di cura, con i medici e i luoghi coinvolti e il motivo indicato, comprese le visite sensibili.
description.pt-BR: Suas consultas, internações e outros atendimentos, com os médicos e locais envolvidos e o motivo informado, incluindo atendimentos sensíveis.

description.en: What a professional you share data with says one of your entries should have been, and why. Your entries are never changed: you decide whether to apply a correction.
description.fr: Ce qu'un professionnel avec qui vous partagez des données dit qu'une de vos saisies aurait dû être, et pourquoi. Vos saisies ne sont jamais modifiées : vous décidez d'appliquer ou non une correction.
description.es: Lo que un profesional con quien comparte datos dice que uno de sus registros debería haber sido, y por qué. Sus registros nunca se modifican: usted decide si aplica una corrección.

description.en: How many children you have.
description.fr: Le nombre d'enfants que vous avez.
description.es: Cuántos hijos tiene.
description.it: Quanti figli ha.
description.pt-BR: Quantos filhos você tem.

description.en: Your menstrual cycles, fertile days and ovulation, your sexual activity and any protection used, whether you are trying to conceive or to avoid a pregnancy, ovulation and pregnancy tests, and your pregnancies and births, including miscarriages and abortions.
description.fr: Vos cycles menstruels, jours fertiles et ovulation, votre activité sexuelle et la protection utilisée, votre intention de concevoir ou d'éviter une grossesse, les tests d'ovulation et de grossesse, et vos grossesses et accouchements, y compris les fausses couches et les interruptions de grossesse.
description.es: Sus ciclos menstruales, días fértiles y ovulación, su actividad sexual y la protección utilizada, si busca un embarazo o intenta evitarlo, las pruebas de ovulación y de embarazo, y sus embarazos y partos, incluidos los abortos espontáneos y las interrupciones del embarazo.
description.it: I suoi cicli mestruali, i giorni fertili e l'ovulazione, la sua attività sessuale e l'eventuale protezione utilizzata, se sta cercando di concepire o di evitare una gravidanza, i test di ovulazione e di gravidanza, e le sue gravidanze e i suoi parti, compresi aborti spontanei e interruzioni di gravidanza.
description.pt-BR: Seus ciclos menstruais, dias férteis e ovulação, sua atividade sexual e a proteção usada, se você está tentando engravidar ou evitando a gravidez, testes de ovulação e de gravidez, e suas gestações e partos, incluindo abortos espontâneos e abortos induzidos.

description.en: Results of genetic tests, such as the gene variants a laboratory tested. Never included when you share all your data: shared only when you name them.
description.fr: Résultats de tests génétiques, comme les variants de gènes testés par un laboratoire. Jamais inclus quand vous partagez toutes vos données : partagés seulement si vous les nommez.
description.es: Resultados de pruebas genéticas, como las variantes de genes analizadas por un laboratorio. Nunca se incluyen cuando comparte todos sus datos: solo se comparten cuando usted los nombra.
description.it: Risultati di test genetici, come le varianti di geni testate da un laboratorio. Mai inclusi quando condivide tutti i suoi dati: condivisi solo quando li nomina.
description.pt-BR: Resultados de testes genéticos, como as variantes de genes testadas por um laboratório. Nunca incluídos quando você compartilha todos os seus dados: compartilhados apenas quando você os indica pelo nome.

description.en: Lets Health Data Safe send you research invitations and eligibility tests. Holds none of your health records: only the score ranges you choose to send and the topics you choose. Never included when you share all your data: shared only when you name it.
description.fr: Permet à Health Data Safe de vous envoyer des invitations à la recherche et des tests d'éligibilité. Ne contient aucun de vos dossiers de santé : seulement les fourchettes de score que vous choisissez d'envoyer et les sujets que vous choisissez. Jamais inclus quand vous partagez toutes vos données : partagé seulement si vous le nommez.

description.en: The score range of each eligibility test you chose to send (below 50%, or 50% and more). Never the exact result or your answers.
description.fr: La fourchette de score de chaque test d'éligibilité que vous avez choisi d'envoyer (moins de 50 %, ou 50 % et plus). Jamais le résultat exact ni vos réponses.

description.en: The research topics you chose, to receive the invitations that concern you.
description.fr: Les sujets de recherche que vous avez choisis, pour recevoir les invitations qui vous concernent.

label.en: Health Data Safe support (holds no data)
label.fr: Assistance Health Data Safe (ne contient aucune donnée)
label.es: Soporte de Health Data Safe (no contiene datos)
label.it: Assistenza Health Data Safe (non contiene dati)
label.pt-BR: Suporte do Health Data Safe (não contém dados)

description.en: Lets the Health Data Safe team exchange messages with you. It holds none of your data.
description.fr: Permet à l'équipe Health Data Safe d'échanger des messages avec vous. Ne contient aucune de vos données.
description.es: Permite que el equipo de Health Data Safe intercambie mensajes con usted. No contiene ninguno de sus datos.
description.it: Permette al team di Health Data Safe di scambiare messaggi con lei. Non contiene nessuno dei suoi dati.
description.pt-BR: Permite que a equipe do Health Data Safe troque mensagens com você. Não contém nenhum dado seu.

description.en: Your use of tobacco and nicotine, how often and how much alcohol you drink, and your diet, including foods you avoid for reasons of belief or health.
description.fr: Votre consommation de tabac, de nicotine et d'alcool, et votre alimentation, y compris les aliments que vous évitez par conviction ou pour raison de santé.
description.es: Su consumo de tabaco y nicotina, con qué frecuencia y cuánto alcohol bebe, y su alimentación, incluidos los alimentos que evita por creencias o por motivos de salud.
description.it: Il suo consumo di tabacco e nicotina, con quale frequenza e in che quantità beve alcol, e la sua alimentazione, compresi gli alimenti che evita per convinzione o per motivi di salute.
description.pt-BR: Seu uso de tabaco e nicotina, com que frequência e quanto álcool você bebe, e a sua alimentação, incluindo alimentos que você evita por crença ou por saúde.

description.en: Your other names, such as a usage name, your name at birth or a former name, so that your app recognises your documents.
description.fr: Vos autres noms, comme un nom d'usage, votre nom de naissance ou un ancien nom, pour que votre app reconnaisse vos documents.
description.es: Sus otros nombres, como un nombre de uso, su nombre de nacimiento o un nombre anterior, para que su app reconozca sus documentos.

description.en: Who you are: your name, display name and photo, date of birth, sex, ethnicity, country of birth and of residence, your reproductive stage, such as pregnancy or menopause, and your account preferences such as language and time zone.
description.fr: Qui vous êtes : vos nom et prénom, nom d'affichage et photo, date de naissance, sexe, origine ethnique, pays de naissance et de résidence, votre stade reproductif, comme la grossesse ou la ménopause, et les préférences de votre compte comme la langue et le fuseau horaire.
description.es: Quién es usted: su nombre, nombre visible y foto, fecha de nacimiento, sexo, origen étnico, país de nacimiento y de residencia, su etapa reproductiva, como el embarazo o la menopausia, y las preferencias de su cuenta, como el idioma y la zona horaria.
description.it: Chi è: il suo nome, il nome visualizzato e la foto, la data di nascita, il sesso, l'origine etnica, il paese di nascita e di residenza, la sua fase riproduttiva, come la gravidanza o la menopausa, e le preferenze del suo account come la lingua e il fuso orario.
description.pt-BR: Quem você é: seu nome, nome de exibição e foto, data de nascimento, sexo, etnia, país de nascimento e de residência, sua fase reprodutiva, como gravidez ou menopausa, e as preferências da sua conta, como idioma e fuso horário.

description.en: The questionnaires you were asked to answer and your answers: for each question, whether you answered yes or no, did not know or preferred not to say, with any detail you added and the reason you gave for not answering, on any health topic. The records your answers point to are shared separately. Never included when you share all your data: shared only when you name them.
description.fr: Les questionnaires auxquels on vous a demandé de répondre et vos réponses : pour chaque question, si vous avez répondu oui ou non, si vous ne saviez pas ou si vous avez préféré ne pas répondre, avec les précisions que vous avez ajoutées et la raison que vous avez donnée pour ne pas répondre, sur tout sujet de santé. Les données auxquelles vos réponses renvoient sont partagées séparément. Jamais inclus quand vous partagez toutes vos données : partagés seulement si vous les nommez.
description.es: Los cuestionarios que se le pidió responder y sus respuestas: para cada pregunta, si respondió sí o no, si no lo sabía o si prefirió no decirlo, con los detalles que añadió y el motivo que dio para no responder, sobre cualquier tema de salud. Los registros a los que remiten sus respuestas se comparten por separado. Nunca se incluyen cuando comparte todos sus datos: solo se comparten cuando usted los nombra.
description.it: I questionari a cui le è stato chiesto di rispondere e le sue risposte: per ogni domanda, se ha risposto sì o no, se non sapeva o se ha preferito non rispondere, con i dettagli che ha aggiunto e il motivo che ha dato per non rispondere, su qualsiasi argomento di salute. I dati a cui rimandano le sue risposte sono condivisi separatamente. Mai inclusi quando condivide tutti i suoi dati: condivisi solo quando li nomina.
description.pt-BR: Os questionários que pediram para você responder e as suas respostas: para cada pergunta, se você respondeu sim ou não, não soube ou preferiu não dizer, com os detalhes que você acrescentou e o motivo que deu para não responder, sobre qualquer assunto de saúde. Os registros para os quais as suas respostas apontam são compartilhados separadamente. Nunca incluídos quando você compartilha todos os seus dados: compartilhados apenas quando você os indica pelo nome.

description.en: The questionnaires you were asked to answer: their questions, on any health topic, and who asked. Never included when you share all your data: shared only when you name them.
description.fr: Les questionnaires auxquels on vous a demandé de répondre : leurs questions, sur tout sujet de santé, et qui les a posées. Jamais inclus quand vous partagez toutes vos données : partagés seulement si vous les nommez.
description.es: Los cuestionarios que se le pidió responder: sus preguntas, sobre cualquier tema de salud, y quién las formuló. Nunca se incluyen cuando comparte todos sus datos: solo se comparten cuando usted los nombra.
description.it: I questionari a cui le è stato chiesto di rispondere: le loro domande, su qualsiasi argomento di salute, e chi le ha poste. Mai inclusi quando condivide tutti i suoi dati: condivisi solo quando li nomina.
description.pt-BR: Os questionários que pediram para você responder: suas perguntas, sobre qualquer assunto de saúde, e quem os enviou. Nunca incluídos quando você compartilha todos os seus dados: compartilhados apenas quando você os indica pelo nome.

description.en: Your answers to questionnaires: for each question, whether you answered yes or no, did not know or preferred not to say, with any detail you added and the reason you gave for not answering, on any health topic. The records your answers point to are shared separately. Never included when you share all your data: shared only when you name them.
description.fr: Vos réponses aux questionnaires : pour chaque question, si vous avez répondu oui ou non, si vous ne saviez pas ou si vous avez préféré ne pas répondre, avec les précisions que vous avez ajoutées et la raison que vous avez donnée pour ne pas répondre, sur tout sujet de santé. Les données auxquelles vos réponses renvoient sont partagées séparément. Jamais incluses quand vous partagez toutes vos données : partagées seulement si vous les nommez.
description.es: Sus respuestas a los cuestionarios: para cada pregunta, si respondió sí o no, si no lo sabía o si prefirió no decirlo, con los detalles que añadió y el motivo que dio para no responder, sobre cualquier tema de salud. Los registros a los que remiten sus respuestas se comparten por separado. Nunca se incluyen cuando comparte todos sus datos: solo se comparten cuando usted los nombra.
description.it: Le sue risposte ai questionari: per ogni domanda, se ha risposto sì o no, se non sapeva o se ha preferito non rispondere, con i dettagli che ha aggiunto e il motivo che ha dato per non rispondere, su qualsiasi argomento di salute. I dati a cui rimandano le sue risposte sono condivisi separatamente. Mai incluse quando condivide tutti i suoi dati: condivise solo quando le nomina.
description.pt-BR: Suas respostas aos questionários: para cada pergunta, se você respondeu sim ou não, não soube ou preferiu não dizer, com os detalhes que você acrescentou e o motivo que deu para não responder, sobre qualquer assunto de saúde. Os registros para os quais as suas respostas apontam são compartilhados separadamente. Nunca incluídas quando você compartilha todos os seus dados: compartilhadas apenas quando você as indica pelo nome.

allergy-coded.devNotes: event.time is the onset, at its precision (PARTIAL-DATES.md); hdsTimePrecision: unknown when the person does not know it. No duration in v1: time + duration is reserved for an abatement, as on condition-coded, and an event that carries one is refused by the FHIR rendering. `status` is required: the item format has no default value, so the entry UI presets it to active; a writer that is not a form (a bridge, the MCP import) states it and never defaults it. `verificationStatus` absent = not stated; never defaulted to confirmed. `reactions` (allergy/coded-v1) is not a form field: an array of objects, which no composite field type holds (as procedure `findings`); a writer that has reactions writes them itself, and the entry UI adds a repeating group later, the stored shape being fixed now. At least one code (`allergen.codes` minItems 1): an allergen no code was found for is allergy-basic. The entry UI must write no `categories` key for an empty multi-select, never `categories: []` (minItems 1), and must write `lastOccurrence` as YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD, never a full ISO datetime, with a way to enter a year or a month alone (a plain date widget allows neither). An allergy pass as a document is the `allergy-record` document kind (documentKinds.yaml), on `documents`, not here. "No known allergy" is its own item (allergy-none-known), never an allergen. See documentation/ALLERGY.md.

Same stream, so one consent unit covers both. Every other field, and every rule of allergy-coded's devNotes (onset, no duration in v1, status stated by every writer, verification never defaulted to confirmed, reactions not a form field, no empty `categories` and `lastOccurrence` written as YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD by the entry UI), applies unchanged.

No duration. `scope` is required and has no default: the entry UI asks for it. `verificationStatus` absent = not stated; never defaulted to confirmed; an import keeps the source's value. No status, categories, type, criticality, lastOccurrence or reactions: the eventType refuses them. Whether a statement is still current (the latest one for its scope, and no active allergy within its scope) is judged by readers, by one shared function in hds-fhir-js, never stored here. condition-coded.devNotes: event.time is the onset (or the diagnosis date when that is all the source knows). Optional content.status is the FHIR clinicalStatus code (active, recurrence, relapse, inactive, remission, resolved); absent = not stated. An abated condition carries event.duration, time + duration being the abatement, and then status must be inactive, remission or resolved (FHIR con-4). No abatement is no duration key: never 0, never null. An abatement within one period with the onset is not stored (the core reads a duration of 0 back as absent): the abated status is kept, with no duration and no hdsEndPrecision (4.11.1, CONDITION.md). Partial onset and abatement dates follow PARTIAL-DATES.md (hdsTimePrecision, hdsEndPrecision). content.verificationStatus is reserved for the FHIR verification status (not stored yet). See documentation/CONDITION.md.

consent-record.devNotes: Append-only history of the account-level consents (plan 91): one event per act, never updated in place; the current state of a document is its latest event. Written by the account app with the personal token at signup, at re-consent and from the Privacy & Consents center. Withdrawing `health-processing` (or `us-chd-consent` under US residence) is account deletion: export, then delete, no event written. An optional choice (the research opt-in) records yes as `given` and no as `declined`, or `withdrawn` after a yes; the account stays. No app requests access to this stream. See documentation/CONSENTS.md.

document.devNotes: One event per document: the file (or its pages) as Pryv attachments, the DocumentEntry metadata as content. The kind of document is its class and type codes, not a stream, and the `documents` root is a new root so no existing grant covers it. Not entered through a form: the person imports a file (forms show "not editable here"). A replacement is a new event listing the old one in `supersedes`. FHIR: a DocumentReference whose files are Binary resources (the `fhir` block, 4.2.0; IPS has no DocumentReference profile). See documentation/DOCUMENTS.md.

encounter-visit.devNotes: Forms enter kind, reason and notes; importers also write specialty, participants and serviceProvider, which an edit keeps. event.time is when the visit began and event.duration how long it lasted. The duration block allows null because a stay can be ongoing (FHIR status in-progress); a writer that does not know the end writes no duration at all, never null, or the visit would read in-progress forever. Status is derived, never stored. Typed ids in content, each mirrored in clientData.related (PROVENANCE.md). No references: no SNOMED / LOINC concept is the record itself. No fhir block yet (Encounter needs a renderer first). See documentation/ENCOUNTER.md.

fertility-cycles-average-peak-day.devNotes:
The recalled average cycle day of the mucus Peak Day, the same Peak Day as `fertility-cycles-peak-day`
(meaning fixed in 3.24.0, B-2026-10-26-19): never an LH peak, a fertility monitor's Peak reading or
ovulation. The value is a cycle day number (day 1 = the `fertility-cycles-start` day), stored on
`time/d`. A recalled summary: one event, `time` at the date the answer is given
(MENSTRUAL-CYCLE.md § Recalled summaries). Chart notation as the person recalls it, not a statement
of fertility. v2 since 4.11.0 (B-2026-10-28-7): v1 said "typical cycle day of peak fertility", so an
answer given before 4.11.0 may be an LH or monitor peak. No LH twin: a recalled average LH peak day
is never written here; it gets its own item if an intake ever asks for it.

fertility-cycles-regularity.devNotes: A recalled summary of the cycles in the person's own words, beside the fertility-cycles-average-* family (site-agents#39): one event per answer, `time` at the date it is given (MENSTRUAL-CYCLE.md § Cycle regularity). For a person who charts, regularity can be derived from fertility-cycles-start; this item is for the answer given without a chart, and a reader prefers the derived value when both exist. "Not sure" is no answer and is not recorded. `no-periods` is what the person reports, never a diagnosis: do not derive amenorrhoea (a condition-coded entry) or a profile-reproductive-stage from it. SNOMED 364307006 is the observable "Regularity of menstrual cycle"; the option findings, for export, are 302757007 Regular periods and 80182007 Irregular periods; `no-periods` has no code short of 14302001 Amenorrhea, a clinical judgement the person has not stated, so it stays uncoded. That is why the item has no fhir block: a coded block must map every option. Never add one by coding `no-periods` as 14302001.

fertility-cycles-ovulation.devNotes:
One event per cycle, `time` anywhere on the calendar day of ovulation, no duration.
A source writing a *predicted* ovulation (Mira, until the cycle completes) sets
`clientData.hdsBasis: 'predicted'` and updates the same event in place to `'confirmed'` once
known; absent = not stated. Phases are derived from this item (hds-lib `cyclePhaseAt`); it is
never a phase itself (see documentation/MENSTRUAL-CYCLE.md).

fertility-cycles-start.devNotes:
Cycle duration is determined by next fertility cycle date unless duration property is given.
This item is what opens a new cycle;
`fertility-cycles-period-end` records the last day of the bleeding.
On the open (current) cycle, `duration` is always a prediction: only the next start ends a cycle.
Same `clientData.hdsBasis` convention as `fertility-cycles-ovulation`, qualifying `time` (the day).

fertility-cycles-period-end.devNotes:
To track start / end of period, use fertility-cycles-start & fertility-cycles-period-end.

The stream is `fertility-cycles-period`, not the key: kept, a stream rename moves data.
`time` is on the last bleeding day; the period is the `-start` day through this day inclusive.
Same `clientData.hdsBasis` convention as `fertility-cycles-ovulation`.

fertility-cycles-peak-day.devNotes:
The mucus Peak Day of the fertility-awareness methods (Billings, Creighton, FEMM, Marquette,
Sensiplan, STM, Peak Day tracking): the last day of peak-type cervical fluid, in the method's own
terms, known in retrospect once the fluid changes. One event per cycle, `time` anywhere on that
calendar day, no duration. Meaning fixed in 3.24.0 (B-2026-10-26-19): it is never the LH peak
(`fertility-cycles-lh-peak-day`), a fertility monitor's Peak reading, or ovulation
(`fertility-cycles-ovulation`). v2 since 3.24.0: events written before 3.24.0 by Cycle
Intelligence (demo accounts only) may be LH peaks. Chart notation recorded by the person or a
charting app, not a statement of fertility. See documentation/MENSTRUAL-CYCLE.md "Peak days".

description.en: The day your LH surge peaked, on a urine test or a monitor.

fertility-cycles-lh-peak-day.devNotes:
The peak of the luteinizing-hormone surge, as the person (or an app) marks it from urine LH
tests (`fertility-test-opk`, `body-urine-hormones-lh`) or a fertility monitor. One event per
cycle, `time` anywhere on that calendar day, no duration. Distinct from the mucus Peak Day
(`fertility-cycles-peak-day`): the two usually fall a day or two apart and either can be
recorded without the other. Added in 3.24.0 (B-2026-10-26-19). A sibling stream, not a child of
`fertility-cycles-peak-day`, so a permission on one never grants the other. No LOINC or SNOMED
CT concept found for it (2026-10-28). HealthKit has no peak-day sample:
`HKCategoryValueOvulationTestResult.luteinizingHormoneSurge` is a per-test result and maps to
`fertility-test-opk`. FHIR: a locally coded Observation, or omitted.

fertility-cycles-coverline.devNotes:
The basal-temperature coverline of one cycle, in °C. One event per cycle, `time` on the
calendar day of that cycle's `fertility-cycles-start` (the patient's time zone), no duration.
`clientData.hdsBasis` says where the value comes from: 'manual' (the person drew or moved the
line) or 'auto' (computed by the method's coverline rule, see the converter's
`temperatureRule`, and stored as computed); absent = not stated. Precedence, one rule: a
reader that computes the line shows a 'manual' event if there is one, otherwise its own
computation, never a stored 'auto'; a reader that cannot compute shows whichever event exists.
An 'auto' event is written only by the writer that owns the cycle's data (an import), and
replaced by that writer; apps that compute never store 'auto'. Going back to the method's rule
deletes the event. Recommended: `clientData.related.<cycleStartEventId>: true`, so a moved
start does not orphan the line; if the cycle start moves, the writer moves the coverline with
it. Chart notation, never a fertility verdict. Added in 3.24.0; see
documentation/MENSTRUAL-CYCLE.md "Coverline".

description.en: The stamp put on your chart for this day.

fertility-cycles-chart-stamp.devNotes:
The stamp (sticker) a person or her instructor put on a day of a stamp-based chart (Creighton,
Billings), kept as charted (site-agents#67). One event per day and method, `time` anywhere on that
calendar day, no duration. `method` is the charting method's id, as `content.source.key` of a mucus
observation; `stamp` names the whole stamp.
Chart notation, never a fertility verdict: no reader derives a fertile or infertile day from it, and
it is never an input of a conversion or a score. A reader that does not know the method or the stamp
draws its own. It belongs to the day, not to one observation: a day
may hold a stamp and no code. A reader drawing a chart of `method` shows it in place of the stamp it
would draw; it changes no other method's chart. Deleting the event brings the drawn stamp back.
An app never stores a stamp it drew itself (a corrected code would keep the old stamp): only one the
person picked or an import read. `yellow` and `yellow-baby` are used on the instructor's
instruction only, so an app offers them only to a person who asked for them, and never proposes one.
The peak mark (`fertility-cycles-peak-day`) and the count days (derived) are not part of it.
`type: imported` keeps it out of generic pickers and forms: a person enters it in a chart's own
stamp control. Added in 4.32.0; see documentation/MENSTRUAL-CYCLE.md "Charted stamp".

Bands, not months: the edges are the guideline anchors (6, 12, 24 months), and a number would invent precision. `on-break` is a reported status that states no duration. The intention stays on fertility-ttc-tta, a sibling stream so a grant on one never covers the other: an intake writes the current intention there for the four bands, and nothing there for `on-break`. SNOMED 169449001 Trying to conceive (finding). LOINC 64632-3 (PhenX, TRIAL) asks the same question as a number of months, so it is not this item's code; no fhir block (a band needs a range value, which the fhir checker has no kind for).

fertility-pregnancy.devNotes:
One per fetus (can be multiple events sharing the same `time` for multifetal pregnancies).
The value of `event.time` is the patient's LMP (last menstrual period) date for this
pregnancy — standard OB/GYN dating convention. Derivations:
  - estimated conception ≈ time + 14 days
  - estimated delivery   ≈ time + 280 days (40 weeks)
  - outcome date          = time + duration
When content value is 'ongoing', `event.duration` must be `null`.
For any other value, `event.duration` is the elapsed time from LMP to outcome.
Use 'very-early-loss' for losses with `duration < 6 weeks` (biochemical / pre-clinical
pregnancies, typically detected only by hCG without ultrasound confirmation —

lifestyle-tobacco-smoking.devNotes: Coded status, not a severity ratio: never / former / current is the shape SNOMED and FHIR use for smoking status. It is a COARSENING of the US Core Smoking Status value set, which splits current into every-day (449868002) and some-day (428041000124106) and carries two unknown states. Note when exporting: `current` maps to 77176002, whose SNOMED FSN is "Smoker (finding)" but which US Core displays as "Smoker, current status unknown" — a US Core-aware reader will read it as unknown frequency, which is accurate here, since v1 stores no tobacco frequency at all. References 365981007 (Finding of tobacco smoking behavior) rather than the broader 365980008 (Finding of tobacco use and exposure), which also covers passive exposure. Quantity is deliberately absent from v1 — cigarettes per day does not generalise to the e-cigarette and smokeless siblings, and pack-years is derived, which this model keeps on the reader side. Adding a quantity item later is additive; shipping a wrong unit is not reversible.

It selects five of the nine bands lifestyle/frequency-band-v1 offers; the loader validates that every option is in the enum and does not require the item to cover it, which is what lets one shape type serve several instruments. lifestyle-alcohol-typical-quantity.devNotes: Grams of ethanol, not standard drinks: a standard drink is 8 g in the UK (one unit), 10 g in Australia and France, and 14 g in the US, so storing drinks makes cross-cohort comparison silently wrong. The app converts from the local standard drink at entry. Reuses the legacy Pryv `mass/g` rather than a new lifestyle-scoped type — a new one would be numerically identical, which is the equivalence hazard AGENTS.md forbids. `mass/g` itself declares no minimum, so the bound is declared here as the item-level `min: 0`, which the model publishes. Renderers should enforce it; hds-forms-js does not yet (`NumberInput.tsx` ignores it), so a reader should still treat a negative value as invalid. SNOMED 896810008 is "estimated intake of ethanol in grams in 24 hours", a daily observable; this item is per typical DRINKING day, so the mapping is close but not exact.

Its stream is a sibling of `questionnaire-answer`, so each is granted alone (`patient/Questionnaire.rs`, `patient/QuestionnaireResponse.rs`). A grant on this stream reads the question texts of every requester and, on the Pryv API, `content.requester.relationship`, the base id of the access the person gave the requester: an opaque id, meaningful in her account only, accepted here because the root is `explicitGrantOnly` (plan 115, 2026-11-16). The FHIR rendering leaves `requester` out.

audit-log/account.description: A record the server writes about the account itself, in its own audit log. `account.created`: the account was created on this core, the first record of its audit log, written once the account exists (by a registration, by an administrator of the platform, or by a delegate); it is also the record of the account's first personal access, when one was made. `account.deleted`: the account is being erased (by its holder, an administrator, the automatic deletion, a replay of the erasure ledger, or the server rolling back a creation), written before any of its data goes and only where the audit log outlives the account. `account.restored`: the account was restored from a backup, written once the restore keeps it.

consent/request-cmc.description: Cross-account consent request issued by a requester (`cmc/request-v1` lineage). The plugin mints a single-use capability access from this trigger, embeds the URL in `content.capabilityUrl`, and delivers the request to the recipient.

to.description: Recipient identity, or `null` for an open invite to be claimed via the capability URL.

capabilityRequested.description: When true, the plugin mints a single-use capability URL the recipient can open out-of-band.

request.description: The consent assertion: localised title/description/consent text + the requested permissions + optional features and expiry.

title.description: Localized text: language-code (2-3 lowercase letters) → string.

mandatory.description: Consent-layer flag: this entry is required for the requesting app to function - an accept must include it (the consent UI locks it; the user's alternative is denying the whole request).

optIn.description: Consent-layer flag: this entry is optional and the consent UI opens it NOT pre-selected (the user opts in). Omit it for the default, where an optional entry opens pre-selected and the user may opt out. Display-only: it never changes what may be granted, and it cannot be combined with `mandatory` on the same entry.

mandatory.description: Consent-layer flag: this entry is required for the requesting app to function - an accept must include it (the consent UI locks it; the user's alternative is denying the whole request).

optIn.description: Consent-layer flag: this entry is optional and the consent UI opens it NOT pre-selected (the user opts in). Omit it for the default, where an optional entry opens pre-selected and the user may opt out. Display-only: it never changes what may be granted, and it cannot be combined with `mandatory` on the same entry.

expiresAt.description: Absolute expiry of the capability access, Unix timestamp (seconds). Omit for the platform default (7 days). `null` requests a capability without expiry; the core accepts it for `capability.mode: 'open-link'` only and refuses it on single-use invites.

allowUserChoice.description: Default false: the consent is ALL OR NOTHING (the user may only accept the whole permission set or deny). Set true to let the user cherry-pick entries on the consent screen (entries flagged `mandatory` stay locked).

requireVerifiedEmail.description: Default false. Set true when accepting must take a proved email address: the accept is refused (`cmc-verified-email-required`) while the accepting account's primary address is not proved. The permissions must ask `:system:email` at `read`, flagged `mandatory` with `allowUserChoice`; not available to a membership request. Enforced by the accepting platform when its service info has `features.cmcRequireVerifiedEmail`; not a guarantee to the requester, which reads `verification/email` through the grant when it uses the address.

accessType.description: Pryv access type the accepted data-grant is minted as. Default `shared` (a non-delegable grant that cannot call `accesses.*`). Set `app` to make the grant delegable: the approved requester can `accesses.create` scoped, individually-named sub-accesses (permissions ⊆ the grant) for least-privilege re-delegation with per-actor audit attribution.

membership.description: Default false. Set true when the requester asks to join the accepter's group: the access the accepter mints is a membership access (role `member`) through which the member writes `consent/member-access-cmc` on the group's scope streams. Enforced by the platform, on write and again at accept: stream permissions only, on user-creatable `:_cmc:apps:<app>[:<path>]` streams, level `read` or `contribute`; no feature permissions; `accessType` absent or `shared`; `allowUserChoice` is treated as true whatever is sent (the accepter picks the scopes). A violation is refused with `cmc-membership-permissions-invalid`.

consent/accept-cmc.description: Cross-account consent accept (`cmc/accept-v1` lineage). Has two shapes: LOCAL TRIGGER (carries `capabilityUrl`, written by the accepter's app to start the accept flow) OR PEER-DELIVERED (carries `grantedAccess.apiEndpoint` + server-stamped `from`, written by the accepter's plugin to the requester's responses stream / inbox).

capabilityUrl.description: Local-trigger shape: capability URL from the request.

accessName.description: Optional name for the data-grant access the accepter mints.

grantedPermissions.description: Optional consent downgrade: grant only this subset of the request's permissions (exact-entry identity; validated against the offer by the accepter's plugin).

extra.description: Deprecated: ignored by the platform. Use `features`.

features.description: The relationship's channels. On the local trigger: the features the accepter asks for, which can only narrow the offer's (`content.request.features`; each one is on unless set to `false`). The platform resolves the relationship's value from the offer and records it on the completed trigger and on the peer-delivered accept.

grantedAccess.description: Peer-delivered shape: data-grant URL the accepter minted on their account.

from.description: Server-stamped at inbox-write time from the back-channel access's stored counterparty identity.

acceptEventId.description: Peer-delivered shape, server-written: the id of the accepter's accept trigger, on the accepter's account. The requester's core records it on its relationship access, so a later `consent/revoke-cmc` naming an earlier accept does not tear down a relationship re-established since. Absent when the accepter's core predates it.

consent/refuse-cmc.description: Cross-account consent refuse (`cmc/refuse-v1` lineage). Carries the capability URL of the request being refused + an optional localised reason.

consent/revoke-cmc.description: Cross-account consent revoke (`cmc/revoke-v1` lineage). Either party tears down an established access pair by writing this with the local data-grant access id + an optional localised reason. The notice delivered to the counterparty also carries server-written fields, among them the correlation fields `acceptEventId` and `revokedAt` and the relationship identifiers (`appCode`, `scopeStreamId`, `offerEventId`, `inviteEventId`, `from`, `backChannelAccessId` / `dataGrantAccessId`, `revokedAccessIds`; see the cross-account messaging implementer's guide for the full list). An inbox arrival the receiving core dropped as stale is marked `superseded` by the receiving core, never by the sender.

acceptEventId.description: Server-written: the accept the revoked relationship descends from. On a notice sent by the accepter, the accepter's accept trigger id; a receiving core whose relationship pairs with another accept (re-established since) records the notice and tears nothing down. On the accepter's own arrival, the id its accept trigger was stamped with.

revokedAt.description: Server-written on the delivered notice: when the revoke was issued (Unix timestamp, seconds). A notice delivered late (re-sent by the retry loop) keeps accesses the receiver created after this time. Absent when the sender's core predates it.

superseded.description: Server-written on inbox arrivals only (never set by the sender): the receiving core dropped this late notice because the relationship was re-established since (it pairs with a later accept). Nothing was torn down; apps must ignore such an arrival and keep the endpoints they hold for that counterparty and scope. Absent on a notice that was acted upon, and when the receiver's core predates it.

consent/back-channel-cmc.description: Post-acceptance handshake step (`cmc/back-channel-v1` lineage). Delivered from the requester to the accepter's `:_cmc:inbox` via the data-grant URL, carrying the requester's back-channel apiEndpoint + remote stream-ids so the accepter can later POST chat / system messages back to the requester.

consent/scope-request-cmc.description: Collector-proposed scope change on an established consent (`cmc/system-scope-request-v1` lineage). The collector writes a proposal carrying the desired new permissions; the user-side app accepts or refuses by writing a corresponding `consent/scope-update-cmc` event.

optIn.description: Consent-layer flag: this entry is optional and the consent UI opens it NOT pre-selected (the user opts in). Omit it for the default, where an optional entry opens pre-selected and the user may opt out. Display-only: it never changes what may be granted, and it cannot be combined with `mandatory` on the same entry.

consent/scope-update-cmc.description: User-side scope change apply / notify (`cmc/system-scope-update-v1` lineage). Has two shapes: response-to-request (carries `scopeRequestEventId` + `accept`) OR self-initiated (carries `newPermissions`). The plugin updates the local data-grant access permissions and notifies the peer.

Omit it for the default, where an optional entry opens pre-selected and the user may opt out. consent/invalidate-link-cmc.description: Requester-side withdrawal of a consent capability, open-link or single-use (`cmc/invalidate-link-v1` lineage). Written on the invite's stream or an ancestor of it. The plugin flips the capability access state to `'invalidated'` so further accepts are rejected with `cmc-capability-invalidated`. For a single-use invite nobody accepted yet (server 2.0.0-rc.56 and later), the `consent/request-cmc` trigger's `content.status` also becomes `invalidated` (with `invalidatedAt` and `reason`); on a single-use capability already accepted it stays a no-op success. Already-established data-grant + back-channel relationships are UNTOUCHED: use `consent/revoke-cmc` for per-relationship teardown. The offer text stays readable through the link until the capability expires.

consent/member-access-cmc.description: A group member asks the group's core for a short-lived access on a patient's account. Written on the group account, on a scope stream the member's membership access holds `contribute` on (or by the group's personal token). The group's core mints a `shared` child access on the patient's core through the data-grant it holds, named and attributed by the server, and returns its apiEndpoint once, in the `memberAccess` field of the synchronous `events.create` response (never stored on the event). Server-owned fields (`status`, `failure`, `memberAccess`, `member`, `relationshipAccessId`) are written by the platform after dispatch and never by a client: a client-supplied value is discarded on create, and the stored value is kept on update.

counterparty.description: The patient: the counterparty of the group's relationship whose data-grant is used.

host.description: The counterparty's canonical host, as stored on the group's relationship access (`clientData.cmc.counterparty.host`), not the hostname of a per-user API URL.

scopeStreamId.description: Scope stream of the patient relationship. Default: the trigger's stream; must equal it or be under it.

permissions.description: Stream permissions of the child access, a subset of the offer's stream permissions outside `:_cmc:` (level not above the offer's). Default: the offer's stream permissions outside `:_cmc:`, at level `read`. Feature permissions are refused; the patient's core enforces the data-grant as the final bound.

expireAfter.description: Lifetime of the child access, in seconds. Default and bounds are per core (`cmc:memberAccess:defaultTtl`, `minTtl`, `maxTtl`; 24 hours, 60 seconds and 7 days by default), and never beyond the data-grant's own expiry.

status.description: Server-owned: dispatch state of the trigger.

failure.description: Server-owned, present when `status` is `failed`: `reason` is an error id (e.g. `cmc-member-access-grant-not-delegable`, `cmc-member-access-peer-rejected`, `cmc-member-access-peer-unreachable`, `cmc-member-access-membership-gone`, `cmc-member-access-not-retryable`); `detail` carries at most `peerErrorId`, `httpStatus` and `retryAfterMs` (the peer's Retry-After, in milliseconds, when it sent one), never a peer response body.

memberAccess.description: Server-owned, on success: the child access minted on the patient's core. Never carries its token or apiEndpoint.

name.description: Server-derived: `cmc-member--<member-slug>--<hash>`.

attribution.description: `stamped`: the child access carries the member and group identity in its `clientData.cmc`, set by the patient's core. `name-only`: the patient's core runs an older release that refuses the stamp; only the access name identifies the member.

member.description: Server-owned: the member, taken from the membership access that wrote the trigger.

relationshipAccessId.description: Server-owned: id of the group's access for the patient relationship used.

consent/member-revoke-cmc.description: Offboarding of a group member: removes the child accesses minted for that member on patients' cores. Written by the platform on the group's scope stream whenever a membership ends (revoked, deleted, expired, narrowed, delegation detached, account deleted, or found gone by the periodic check); a client write is refused with `cmc-protected-event-write`, and every field is server-owned (a client-supplied value is discarded on create, and the stored value is kept on update). Records who was offboarded and what was removed, with the outcome per child access.

reason.description: What ended the membership. `vanished`: the membership access was found gone by the periodic check while its child accesses remained (deleted by a path that did not offboard, or interrupted before it did). `narrowed`: an `accesses.update` removed teams, or a team stream was deleted (see `uncovered`).

uncovered.description: Server-owned, on a `narrowed` record caused by the deletion of a team stream: the stream(s) deleted. The record is then written on the deleted stream's parent (or `:_cmc:apps`).

status.description: Server-owned: dispatch state of the trigger.

failure.description: Server-owned, present when `status` is `failed`: `reason` is an error id (e.g. `cmc-member-revoke-residual`); `detail` carries at most `childAccessId`, `peerErrorId`, `httpStatus` and `retryAfterMs` (the peer's Retry-After, in milliseconds, when it sent one), never a peer response body.

outcome.description: Server-owned: the result per child access, read back on the patient's core.

result.description: `deleted`: removed now. `absent`: confirmed gone by the patient's core, or expired. `residual`: not confirmed gone (the patient's core unreachable or refusing, or the access made through another grant); retried, and bounded by the child's own expiry.

reason.description: Why a `residual` or `absent` result was reached, e.g. `peer-rejected`, `grant-gone`, `grant-replaced`, `grant-unknown`.

residuals.description: Server-owned: the child accesses that could not be removed.

expires.description: Unix timestamp (seconds): the latest the residual can live.

contact/facebook.description: A Facebook user as specified in the Graph API: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/reference/api/user/

contact/vcard.description: A business card in vCard 2.0-3.x format. See: rfc2425, rfc2426.

count/generic.description: For general items that demand no particular handling.

credentials/pryv-api-endpoint.description: Necessary information to access a Pryv.io account. Url in the format of http(s)://{token}@{apiEndpoint}

email/string.description: An email address as a plain string, e.g. the account email address. Whether ownership of the account address was proved is given by the accompanying `verification/email` event, returned when requested by type.

encrypted/aes-256-gcm.description: AES-256-GCM encrypted payload. payload is Base64( iv || ciphertext || tag ) where iv is a random 96-bit (12-byte) nonce generated per encryption, ciphertext is the AES-256-GCM encryption of the UTF-8 JSON plaintext, and tag is the 128-bit (16-byte) GCM authentication tag. The key is 256 bits (32 bytes). Standard (non-URL-safe) Base64.

payload.description: The encrypted data: Base64( iv[12] || ciphertext || tag[16] ).

keyRef.description: A reference (e.g. id, name in a keyring) to the key to use for decryption.

hint.description: Alternative or complement to keyRef. A hint about which key to use for decryption.

encrypted/ecies-aes-256-gcm.description: Asymmetric (ECIES-style) encrypted payload for a NIST P-256 (secp256r1) recipient key pair. Encryption: generate an ephemeral P-256 key pair; compute the ECDH shared secret with the recipient's public key (the 32-byte X coordinate); derive the content key with HKDF-SHA-256 (salt: empty, info: the ASCII string encrypted/ecies-aes-256-gcm, output: 32 bytes) and use it as an AES-256-GCM key with a random 96-bit IV. payload is Base64( ephemeralPublicKey || iv || ciphertext || tag ) where ephemeralPublicKey is the 65-byte uncompressed SEC1 point (0x04 || X || Y), iv is 12 bytes and tag is the 16-byte GCM authentication tag. Decryption requires the recipient's private key. Standard (non-URL-safe) Base64.

payload.description: The encrypted data: Base64( ephemeralPublicKey[65] || iv[12] || ciphertext || tag[16] ).

keyRef.description: A reference (e.g. id, name in a keyring) to the recipient key pair whose private key decrypts the payload.

hint.description: Alternative or complement to keyRef. A hint about which key to use for decryption.

encrypted/aes-text-base64.description: DEPRECATED — prefer encrypted/aes-256-gcm. AES encrypted payload, with a text key and a Base64 payload; the exact cipher parameters (mode, key derivation, IV handling) were never fully specified, so implementations may not interoperate.

keyRef.description: A reference (e.g. id, name in keychain) to the key to use for decryption.

hint.description: Alternative to keyRef. A textual hint about which key to use for decryption.

file/attached.description: The file is attached to the event

file/attached-multiple.description: A set of file attached. Structure can be declared in the filenames.

frequency/hz.description: Hertz (also known as cycles per second)

message/facebook.description: A Facebook post. See [Facebook's API docs](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/reference/api/post/) for reference. Facebook properties `message` and `created_time` map to event `description` and `time` respectively. Facebook attached pictures can be directly mapped to attachments. Other Facebook properties such as `link`, `source`, `privacy` are allowed.

properties.description: Relative to `source`: a list of properties for an uploaded video, for example, the length of the video.

picture.description: Either a fully qualified "URL" for an external picture or a "filename" for a picture attached to this event.

status-type.description: One of mobile_status_update, created_note, added_photos, added_video, shared_story, created_group, created_event, wall_post, app_created_story, published_story, tagged_in_photo, approved_friend

title.description: Localized text: language-code (2-3 lowercase letters) → string.

code.description: Optional app-defined code identifying the alert kind (used for grouping / dedup).

ackRequired.description: When true, the recipient is expected to send a `notification/ack-cmc` event back.

ackId.description: Optional explicit ack-id. When absent, the alert event-id is used as the ack reference.

notification/ack-cmc.description: CMC system alert acknowledgement (`cmc/system-ack-v1` lineage). The recipient of a `notification/alert-cmc` writes one of these back referencing the original alert via `alertEventId` + `ackId`.

picture/attached.description: The picture is the image file attached to the event (no explicit content defined). TODO: list accepted formats.

picture/url.description: A reference to a picture file online.

position/wgs84.description: The latest revision of the World Geodetic System (used by GPS).

latitude.description: Unit: degrees north from the equator.

longitude.description: Unit: degrees east from the zero meridian.

horizontalAccuracy.description: The radius of uncertainty for latitude and longitude. Unit: meters. Negative if latitude and longitude are invalid.

verticalAccuracy.description: The radius of uncertainty for altitude. Unit: meters. Negative if altitude is invalid.

speed.description: For informational purposes only. Unit: meters / second. Negative if invalid.

bearing.description: Unit: degrees clockwise from north. Negative if invalid.

reproductive-health/sexual-activity.description: A type to record sexual activity

reproductive-health/menstrual-flow.description: A type to record the menstrual cycles

reproductive-health/mucus-quality.description: A type to record the quality of the mucus

reproductive-health/ovulation.description: A type to record the result of an ovulation test

shared-secret/item.description: One shared secret. Lives under the reserved `:_shared-secrets:<accessId>` stream of the access that created it. The event's own `time` + `duration` carry the lifetime — expiry is exactly `now > time + duration` — and `trashed` marks an item that has left the `pending` state.

keyHash.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the key's random half. The key itself is returned once, at creation, and is never stored — so it cannot be recovered from a database dump or a backup.

title.description: Human-readable label for the account owner, describing what is being shared and with whom.

status.description: `pending` is the only state from which the secret can be retrieved; the other two are terminal.

statusHistory.description: Append-only trail of state transitions, oldest first.

info.description: Why the item was discarded — e.g. `expired`, `deleted`, or a signature mismatch.

onConsumed.description: Shown to whoever presents the key once the secret is no longer available.

returnUrl.description: Where to send the visitor afterwards. Restricted to http(s) — it is followed by an unauthenticated third party.

signature.description: Optional proof required to redeem. `secret` compares a passphrase supplied out-of-band; `hmac-sha256` verifies HMAC(verifier-secret, key material) computed by the client, so the verifier secret itself never reaches the server. A wrong proof discards the secret. `value` is present only while the item is `pending`: it is scrubbed alongside the secret once the item is consumed or discarded (for a `secret`-type signature it is a passphrase in clear), leaving only the `type` on the record.

secret.description: The payload handed over on redemption — any JSON value. Present only while `status` is `pending`: it is removed as soon as the item is consumed or discarded, so a spent secret stops living in backups and exports.

symptoms/severity.description: A type to record severity of a symptom such as bloating or abdominal cramps.

symptoms/appetite-changes.description: A type to represent change in appetite.

verification/email.description: The verification state of the account email address. It accompanies the account email event (same stream, type `email/string`) and is returned when requested by type (`verification/email` or `verification/*`): a read of that stream without types returns the email event only. `verified` describes the address currently in that email event and is the answer to rely on; `method` and `verifiedAt` say how and when, and the list of methods may grow without changing what `verified` means.

verified.description: `true` only when ownership of the address was proved: the holder clicked a one-time link mailed to it (`email-link`), pasted a one-time code mailed to it at registration (`email-code`), or the platform operator marked it verified (`operator`). `false` in every other case, including an address given at registration without proof (`registration`) and an address set without proof by an earlier version of the platform (`legacy`).

method.description: How the current state was reached. `email-link`, `email-code` and `operator` come with `verified: true`; `registration` (the founding address, not proved) and `legacy` (set without proof) come with `verified: false`. `null` when no method is recorded.

verifiedAt.description: When ownership was proved, Unix timestamp (seconds). `null` when the address is not proved or the time is unknown.

video/attached.description: The video is the file attached to the event (no explicit content defined). TODO: list accepted formats.

video/url.description: A reference to an video file online.

vulva-mucus-inspect/v0.description: DEPRECATED — use vulva-mucus-inspect/9d-vector with converter engine instead. Legacy simple enum kept for backward compatibility with existing data.

vulva-mucus-inspect/9d-vector.description: Cervical fluid observation as a 9-dimensional vector. Content is { vectors, source? }. Used with the euclidian-distance converter engine.

source.description: Provenance and method-specific qualifiers: which method produced this vector, and what qualifies its observation (`annotations`). Absent = direct vector input.

key.description: Source method identifier (e.g. mira, chartneo, creighton)

sourceData.description: Raw observation from the source method

annotations.description: Values that qualify the source observation without being part of it, keyed by the id of an annotation of the method's notation (converter pack `notation.annotations`), e.g. Creighton { "frequency": "X2" }. Scoped to the method named by `key`: a writer that changes `key` drops them. Not in the vector, never used by a conversion. Optional for validity: `requiredAtEntry` and `notFor` on the annotation are entry-form rules only, so events stored before it, imported or converted from another method have none and stay valid. An editor that does not know annotations may drop them when it rewrites `source`.

attributes/ethnicity.description: Self-identified ethnicity / race categories, recorded as an epidemiological variable (health-equity monitoring), NOT as a clinical or biological one. One combined self-identified field, deliberately not split into separate race and ethnicity items — see the note below. Array: several categories may apply at once. Maps losslessly onto FHIR US Core at the boundary: 'hispanic-latino' / 'not-hispanic-latino' populate us-core-ethnicity.ombCategory, every other value populates us-core-race.ombCategory. NOTE: 'hispanic-latino' and 'not-hispanic-latino' are the two answers to one question and are mutually exclusive — the array shape cannot enforce that, so writers must not emit both. 'middle-eastern-north-african' is a 2024 SPD-15 category with no OMB-1997 ombCategory code; map it via us-core-race detailed + text.

attributes/reproductive-stage.description: Reproductive-aging / menopausal stage — a durable but time-varying patient attribute, aligned to the STRAW+10 staging system. Selects the reference band for stage-dependent hormones (estradiol, FSH, prolactin). Stage only; hormone therapy is recorded separately as a medication, not encoded here.

fertility/cycle-regularity-v1.description: Self-reported regularity of the menstrual cycles: regular, irregular, or no current periods. A reported summary, not a diagnosis.

fertility/ttc-duration-v1.description: Recalled time trying to conceive, as a band, or a reported break. A reported summary, not a computed duration.

fertility/chart-stamp-v1.description: The stamp (sticker) put on one day of a stamp-based fertility-awareness chart, as charted by the person or her instructor. Chart notation: HDS reads no fertility statement from it, and an HDS app never stores a stamp it computed.

method.description: Identifier of the charting method the stamp belongs to, as `source.key` of a mucus observation (e.g. creighton, billings).

stamp.description: The whole stamp: its colour, `-baby` when it carries a baby.

fertility/tracking-method-v1.description: Fertility-awareness charting methods or devices in use. Determines how the person's cycle observations should be interpreted. Array: several methods run concurrently (a method plus a monitor plus BBT). Each event is a complete dated snapshot of the methods active at that time — a method that stops simply does not appear in the next snapshot.

contact/other-name-v1.description: Another name of the person, beside the given and family names of her profile: a usage name, a birth name, a former name, her full official name, a nickname. FHIR HumanName (given, family, use). At least one of given and family. On the other-names root (explicitGrantOnly): no grant on profile reads it, nor one on * once the production * accesses are masked for it (documentation/PROFILE.md). Her app matches a printed identity against it (documentation/CONVERSATION.md R3); a nickname never matches. See documentation/PROFILE.md.

given.description: Given name(s), one string ('Marie Anne'). FHIR HumanName.given. Absent: her profile's given name goes with this family name.

family.description: Family name. FHIR HumanName.family. Absent: her profile's family name goes with this given name.

use.description: What the name is, FHIR HumanName.use: official (the full name of an identity document), usual (the name she uses, a usage name), maiden (her name at birth, before a marriage), old (a name she no longer uses), nickname (never matched against a document).

ratio/proportion.description: A proportion value from 0 to 1: 0 = none, 1 = maximum.

test-result/scale.description: Generic qualitative test result on a scale from -1 to 1. Negative values indicate a negative result, 0 indicates indeterminate, positive values indicate a positive result. The magnitude represents intensity or confidence. Common values: -1 (negative), 0 (indeterminate), 1 (positive). Intermediate values can represent semi-quantitative results (e.g., 0.5 for a weak positive). Applicable to any binary or semi-quantitative test: medical (OPK, pregnancy, COVID), environmental, industrial, etc.

pregnancy/detailed.description: Pregnancy. Use 'ongoing' while pregnancy is in progress; otherwise the value reflects how it terminated. 'very-early-loss' covers biochemical / pre-clinical losses with duration <6 weeks LMP (typically hCG-detected only, clinically distinct from miscarriage per ESHRE 2022 RPL guideline). 'molar' (hydatidiform mole) is a distinct entity from ectopic — abnormal trophoblastic tissue requiring hCG surveillance.

name.description: The medication's name as written or printed

doseUnit.description: HDS eventType reference for the dose unit

frequency.description: Prescribed frequency (e.g. 2 times per day). Kept structurally identical to the standalone frequency/times-period type; inlined rather than $ref'd because cores compile each event type schema on its own, with no dictionary root to resolve against.

times.description: Number of intakes per period (e.g. 2 for 'twice a day')

period.description: Length of the period (e.g. 1 for 'per day', 8 for 'every 8 hours')

asNeeded.description: True if taken as needed (PRN) rather than on schedule

note.description: Free text instructions (e.g. 'take with food', 'before bedtime')

timeOfDay.description: Clock times of the intakes, the person's local wall-clock time, HH:MM (FHIR Timing.repeat.timeOfDay). Not together with `when`.

when.description: Moments of the day, or times relative to a meal, of the intakes (FHIR Timing.repeat.when, EventTiming). Not together with `timeOfDay`. Labels and FHIR codes: vocabulary medication-when.

bounds.description: Planned course of the regimen (FHIR Timing.repeat.bounds[x]): a length from its start (boundsDuration) or dates (boundsPeriod). Start defaults to the event time. On an intake period, the event's time and duration are the actual period of use; bounds is what was planned. Not the length of each intake (FHIR repeat.duration).

duration.description: Length of the course, from its start

durationUnit.description: Unit of the length (UCUM in FHIR: y is a)

start.description: First day of the course, YYYY-MM-DD

end.description: Last day of the course, YYYY-MM-DD

status.description: State of the prescription (FHIR MedicationRequest.status, R4 and R5: active, stopped, completed). Absent: not stated (FHIR unknown), every event before 3.46.0; absent does not mean active. Labels: vocabulary medication-prescription-status.

statusChanged.description: Day the status took effect, YYYY-MM-DD (FHIR R5 MedicationRequest.statusChanged). Only with status.

stopReason.description: Why it stopped: on an intake period that has ended (ignored on one intake), or on a prescription with status stopped. Absent on an ended period: ended as planned, or not said. FHIR MedicationStatement.statusReason (R4), adherence.reason (R5), MedicationRequest.statusReason. Labels and SNOMED CT codes: vocabulary medication-stop-reason.

name.description: Free-text name of the treatment / regimen (e.g. 'IVF', 'Chemotherapy', 'CBT')

count.description: Aggregate intake count over the patient's lifetime. 0 = never. Use for Flavour A intake capture.

treatment/coded-v1.description: Coded treatment regimen. 'regimen' is the coded identity from datasets-service.

regimen.description: Coded regimen identity, populated from datasets-service selection.

codes.description: Coding identifiers across systems (SNOMED-CT, ICD-10-PCS, CPT, …).

count.description: Aggregate intake count over the patient's lifetime. 0 = never. Use for Flavour A intake capture.

procedure/basic.description: Free-text clinical procedure. 'findings' is an open-vocabulary array describing procedure-bound observations (e.g. endometriosis localisation during a laparoscopy).

name.description: Free-text name of the procedure (e.g. 'Laparoscopy', 'HSG', 'Polypectomy')

count.description: Aggregate intake count (Flavour A: lifetime occurrences). 0 = never.

robotAssisted.description: Procedure was robot-assisted. Absent means not recorded, not false.

findings.description: Open-vocabulary array of procedure-bound observations. Form preset declares which finding types are surfaced per procedure label.

value.description: Finding value — string, boolean, or nested object as appropriate.

procedure/coded-v1.description: Coded clinical procedure. 'procedure' is the coded identity from datasets-service.

procedure.description: Coded procedure identity, populated from datasets-service selection.

codes.description: Coding identifiers across systems (SNOMED-CT, ICD-10-PCS, CPT, …).

robotAssisted.description: Procedure was robot-assisted. Absent means not recorded, not false.

condition/coded-v1.description: Coded clinical diagnosis / condition. 'condition' is the coded identity from datasets-service. Records what the patient HAS (an established diagnosis), distinct from symptoms, procedures and treatments.

condition.description: Coded condition identity, populated from datasets-service selection.

status.description: Condition.clinicalStatus code (FHIR condition-clinical); absent = not stated. With a duration (abated): inactive, remission or resolved.

allergy/coded-v1.description: Coded allergy or intolerance (FHIR AllergyIntolerance). 'allergen' is the coded substance from datasets-service. event.time is the onset; no duration (reserved for an abatement).

allergen.description: Coded allergen (a substance, a drug ingredient or a drug class), populated from datasets-service selection.

hdsId.description: HDS identifier of the picked search result, as datasets-service returns it (the hdsId of its primary code). Never constructed.

codes.description: Coding identifiers across systems (SNOMED-CT, RxNorm, …). At least one: an allergen with no code is allergy/basic-v1.

status.description: AllergyIntolerance.clinicalStatus code (FHIR allergyintolerance-clinical). Required: a writer states it, never defaults it.

verificationStatus.description: AllergyIntolerance.verificationStatus code (FHIR allergyintolerance-verification); absent = not stated, never defaulted to confirmed.

reactions.description: Reactions to the allergen, each an AllergyIntolerance.reaction.

manifestations.description: What the reaction was (reaction.manifestation, 1..*): a datasets-service selection (label, codes) or a text.

lastOccurrence.description: Date of the last known reaction (AllergyIntolerance.lastOccurrence), at its precision: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.

allergy/basic-v1.description: Allergy or intolerance to an allergen entered as free text (FHIR AllergyIntolerance). event.time is the onset; no duration (reserved for an abatement).

name.description: The allergen as written: a name no code was found for.

status.description: AllergyIntolerance.clinicalStatus code (FHIR allergyintolerance-clinical). Required: a writer states it, never defaults it.

verificationStatus.description: AllergyIntolerance.verificationStatus code (FHIR allergyintolerance-verification); absent = not stated, never defaulted to confirmed.

reactions.description: Reactions to the allergen, each an AllergyIntolerance.reaction.

manifestations.description: What the reaction was (reaction.manifestation, 1..*): a datasets-service selection (label, codes) or a text.

lastOccurrence.description: Date of the last known reaction (AllergyIntolerance.lastOccurrence), at its precision: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD.

allergy/none-known-v1.description: No known allergy (FHIR AllergyIntolerance with a SNOMED CT 'no known allergy' code): to anything (scope all) or to one kind of allergen. event.time is when the statement was made, never an onset; no duration. Not an allergy: no status, categories, type, criticality, lastOccurrence or reactions.

scope.description: What the statement covers: all (no known allergy), medication, food or environment (no known allergy of that kind). Each renders as its own SNOMED CT code.

verificationStatus.description: AllergyIntolerance.verificationStatus code (FHIR allergyintolerance-verification); absent = not stated, never defaulted to confirmed.

finding/coded-v1.description: Coded clinical finding. 'finding' is the coded identity from datasets-service. Records what was FOUND at surgery or on imaging (e.g. hydrosalpinx, ovarian endometrioma) — neither a procedure, a symptom, nor quite a diagnosis.

finding.description: Coded finding identity, populated from datasets-service selection.

frequency/times-period.description: Number of times per period. E.g. 2 times per day, 1 time per week.

times.description: Number of intakes per period (e.g. 2 for 'twice a day')

period.description: Length of the period (e.g. 1 for 'per day', 8 for 'every 8 hours')

settings/preferred-locales.description: User preferred locales, ordered by priority

settings/preferred-display.description: One display preference of the user, written by hds-lib HDSSettings for the dynamic setting key 'preferred-display-<itemKey>': one event per itemKey on the application's baseStream, updated in place and deleted when the preference is cleared. The value's shape is owned by the app that sets it (a converter method id, a flag, an object of view preferences), so it is not enforced here.
